t.E351.agn: JECFA set the group ADI for malic acid and its sodium, potassium and calcium salts as 'not specified'; it reported that for D(-)-malic acid and its salts this ADI does not apply to very young infants. EFSA's re-evaluation in the EU is ongoing (a call for data was published in 2024).
t.E351.body: Malic acid is an intermediate of the body's energy cycle (Krebs cycle); the metabolism of the L(+) form is well known, while less is known about the fate of the D(-) form in the body.
t.E351.eff.1.t: The daily limit for D(-)-malic acid and its salts does not apply to very young infants
t.E351.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E351.prod: DL-malic acid is produced by chemical synthesis from petrochemical raw materials; its salts are obtained by neutralisation.
t.E351.pw.0: JECFA has recommended that D(-)- and DL-malic acid not be added to foods for very young infants other than for therapeutic purposes.
t.E351.regx.0: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was published in 2024 (deadline 31.12.2024).
t.E351.regx.1: Group I additive; permitted at quantum satis in many foods.
t.E351.regx.2: ADI not specified (potassium hydrogen DL-malate; group ADI for malic acid and its salts).
t.E351.regx.3: ADI not specified (potassium DL-malate solution; group ADI for malic acid and its salts).
t.E351.summary: The potassium salt of malic acid. Used as an acidity regulator.
t.E351.what: The potassium salt of malic acid; it regulates the acidity of food.
